_doc: Field-wide milestones for the timeline (course-specific events live in each course.json). year < 0 means BC.

milestones.title: Markov’s chains of letters
milestones.detail: Markov showed that each letter of Pushkin’s *Eugene Onegin* depends on the letter before it, the first statistical model of language.

milestones.title: Information theory
milestones.detail: Shannon founded information theory, defining entropy and modelling English as a statistical source — the framework in which language models are still trained and scored.

milestones.title: Computing machinery and intelligence
milestones.detail: Turing proposed judging whether a machine can think by whether it can hold a conversation indistinguishable from a person’s — the imitation game, later called the Turing test.

milestones.title: The Dartmouth workshop
milestones.detail: A summer workshop at Dartmouth College, proposed by McCarthy, Minsky, Rochester and Shannon, gave artificial intelligence its name as a field.

milestones.title: The perceptron
milestones.detail: Rosenblatt’s perceptron learned to classify simple patterns by adjusting its weights after mistakes, the first trainable neural network.

milestones.title: ELIZA
milestones.detail: Weizenbaum’s ELIZA imitated a psychotherapist with simple pattern matching, yet many users attributed understanding to it — an early lesson in how readily people credit machines with minds.

milestones.title: Hopfield networks
milestones.detail: Hopfield showed that a network with symmetric connections can store memories as stable states of an energy function.

milestones.title: Backpropagation
milestones.detail: Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams showed that backpropagation trains multilayer networks to learn their own internal representations.

milestones.title: Statistical machine translation
milestones.detail: Brown and colleagues at IBM learned to translate from French–English parliamentary records with probabilistic models, replacing hand-written rules with statistics learned from data.

milestones.title: Long short-term memory
milestones.detail: Hochreiter and Schmidhuber’s LSTM let recurrent networks carry information across long sequences; it remained the leading sequence model until the Transformer.

milestones.title: Neural language models
milestones.detail: Bengio and colleagues predicted the next word with a neural network over learned word vectors, the ancestor of today’s language models.

milestones.title: Deep belief networks
milestones.detail: Hinton, Osindero and Teh trained deep networks one layer at a time, reviving interest in deep learning.

milestones.title: AlexNet
milestones.detail: A deep convolutional network trained on two GPUs won the ImageNet challenge by a wide margin, and deep learning became the dominant approach to perception.

milestones.title: word2vec
milestones.detail: Mikolov and colleagues learned word vectors from billions of words with a shallow network; their geometry captured meaning and analogy.

milestones.title: Attention
milestones.detail: Bahdanau, Cho and Bengio let a translation model attend to every word of the source sentence, the mechanism at the heart of the Transformer.

milestones.title: AlphaGo
milestones.detail: DeepMind’s AlphaGo, combining deep networks with tree search and reinforcement learning, defeated Lee Sedol at Go.

milestones.title: The Transformer
milestones.detail: Vaswani and colleagues introduced the Transformer, built entirely on attention; it became the architecture of language models.

milestones.title: Learning from human preferences
milestones.detail: Christiano and colleagues trained agents with a reward model learned from human comparisons, the method later used to align language models.

milestones.title: BERT
milestones.detail: Devlin and colleagues’ BERT made pretraining a Transformer on unlabelled text, then fine-tuning it for each task, the standard recipe of NLP.

milestones.title: GPT-3
milestones.detail: A 175-billion-parameter language model learned new tasks from examples in its prompt, showing what scale alone could achieve.

milestones.title: Scaling laws
milestones.detail: Kaplan and colleagues found that language-model loss falls predictably, as a power law, with parameters, data and compute.

milestones.title: Chinchilla
milestones.detail: Hoffmann and colleagues showed that parameters and training data should be scaled together, changing how models are trained.

milestones.title: InstructGPT
milestones.detail: OpenAI fine-tuned GPT-3 with human feedback to follow instructions, the method behind the first chat assistants.

milestones.title: ChatGPT
milestones.detail: OpenAI released ChatGPT as a free research preview; it reached an estimated 100 million users in about two months.

milestones.title: GPT-4
milestones.detail: OpenAI’s GPT-4 accepted images as well as text and performed well on professional and academic exams; its technical report withheld the architecture and training details.

milestones.title: Open-weight models
milestones.detail: Meta’s LLaMA, followed by Llama 2, Mistral, Qwen and many others, put capable language models in the hands of researchers and developers everywhere.

milestones.title: The AI Safety Summit
milestones.detail: At Bletchley Park, 28 countries and the European Union, including the United States and China, signed a declaration on the risks of frontier AI and the need for international cooperation.

milestones.title: Nobel prizes for neural networks
milestones.detail: The Nobel Prize in Physics went to Hopfield and Hinton for foundational work on neural networks, and half of the Chemistry prize to Hassabis and Jumper for predicting protein structures with AlphaFold.
